name: ILTA: The International Legal Technology Association's Website
title: ILTA: The International Legal Technology Association's Website
answer: The International Legal Technology Association is a volunteer-led body for legal technologists with more than 26,000 individual members across over 20 countries. Its website is most useful for its 2026 Technology Survey, which reports input from 508 firms representing over 139,000 lawyers and about 275,000 total users, giving firms data to benchmark their technology implementations and plans. It also carries a foundational AI guide produced with the Thomson Reuters Institute and a press wall of legal technology announcements.

sections.body: The website of the International Legal Technology Association, a volunteer-led association for legal technologists. ILTA reports more than 26,000 individual members, over 100 topic communities, 160 corporate sponsors and members in more than 20 countries. The site combines association material, news and vendor announcements. Its most substantial document is the 2026 Technology Survey, which reports the input of 508 firms representing over 139,000 lawyers and about 275,000 total users. The site also references ILTA's Spring Peer to Peer magazine and a foundational AI guide released with the Thomson Reuters Institute.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The site's central claim about artificial intelligence is that adoption has moved from experiment to something firms can measure and compare. ILTA's Spring Peer to Peer magazine notes that AI has matured rapidly since the early days of large language models in 2023. The 2026 Technology Survey is presented as the instrument for that comparison, giving firms data to benchmark their technology implementations and plans against a large pool of peers. Alongside the survey, ILTA and the Thomson Reuters Institute released a foundational AI guide for legal professionals addressing AI adoption, ethics and professional responsibility across the legal profession. The site's press wall shows how vendors are positioning themselves for that market. NetDocuments is connecting legal knowledge to Microsoft Copilot through an MCP connector, so Copilot answers from an organization's own documents. Opus 2 Ingenuity uses agentic AI to streamline deposition designations for litigation teams. Together these items describe a market where AI is being folded into document and litigation workflows rather than sold as a standalone capability.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: ILTA reports more than 26,000 individual members, over 100 topic communities, 160 corporate sponsors and members in more than 20 countries. The 2026 Technology Survey reports the input of 508 firms representing over 139,000 lawyers and about 275,000 total users. ILTA's Spring Peer to Peer magazine dates the start of the large language model era to 2023 and says AI has matured rapidly since then. The site describes NetDocuments' MCP connector to Microsoft Copilot and Opus 2 Ingenuity's use of agentic AI for deposition designations.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: For a reader following AI in the legal industry, this site is a way to see what firms actually buy and deploy rather than what vendors claim. The 2026 Technology Survey, with 508 firms and roughly 275,000 users behind it, is the kind of benchmark that lets a firm judge whether its own AI plans are ahead of or behind its peers. The foundational AI guide with the Thomson Reuters Institute gives a shared vocabulary for adoption, ethics and professional responsibility. The press wall shows the direction of travel in products, with Copilot connectors and agentic AI for litigation tasks appearing as concrete deployments.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Legal

sections.body: The site is an association and vendor news platform, so much of what it carries is promotional or membership oriented rather than independent research. The survey findings are summarised rather than published in full on the pages read, so the underlying data is not available here. The AI guide is described but its contents are not set out. The press wall items are vendor announcements, not evaluations, and the site gives no independent testing of the products it lists.
